jobs.title: Youth Ministry Summer Internship at Colonial Presbyterian Church
jobs.description: Employer: Colonial Presbyterian Church Expires: 12/10/2026 POSITION SUMMARY The Student Ministry Summer Staff Internship is a nine-week, immersive ministry experience designed to equip college-aged young adults to grow in their relationship with Jesus Christ while gaining hands-on experience serving middle school and high school students. Since 1971, Colonial Presbyterian Church's Summer Staff program has provided opportunities for young adults to live out the Gospel through discipleship, leadership development, and relational ministry. Each summer, approximately 10–15 interns serve across Colonial's two campuses, investing in students while growing personally and spiritually through intentional Christian community. Summer Staff Interns help plan and lead student ministry programs, small groups, and activities that encourage students to know Jesus, grow in their faith, and build meaningful relationships. ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES Student Ministry & Discipleship Build meaningful, Christ-centered relationships with middle school and high school students through mentorship, prayer, and consistent relational ministry. Lead and facilitate small groups, Bible studies, and discipleship opportunities that communicate the Gospel and help students understand and apply Scripture. Encourage students in their spiritual growth while fostering a welcoming, safe environment where they feel known, valued, and supported in their faith. Ministry Programming & Events Assist in planning, organizing, and executing weekly student ministry gatherings, activities, outreach opportunities, and special events. Coordinate event logistics, including setup, supplies, communication, and cleanup, in collaboration with ministry staff and fellow interns. Participate in summer camps, retreats, and other assigned ministry activities that serve students and connect families with Colonial and the surrounding community. Leadership Development & Spiritual Formation Participate in daily devotional time, Bible studies, spiritual disciplines, spiritual formation activities, leadership seminars, and ministry training. Demonstrate a commitment to personal spiritual growth and Christian character in relationships with students, staff, volunteers, and fellow interns. Receive coaching and mentorship from ministry leaders while developing practical skills in leadership, communication, planning, and teamwork. Teamwork & Christian Community Live in Colonial-provided housing with fellow Summer Staff Interns and contribute to a respectful, supportive, and Christ-centered community. Participate in shared community responsibilities, team meetings, and scheduled activities. Work collaboratively with ministry staff and fellow interns demonstrating flexibility, accountability, and a willingness to serve where needed.Take initiative, manage scheduled work hours productively, and fulfill ministry responsibilities independently, including when full-time staff are absent. Represent Colonial Presbyterian Church with integrity both on and off campus. Safety & Ministry Stewardship Follow Colonial's policies and procedures for student safety, supervision, and appropriate boundaries. Complete all required background screenings and ministry safety training before beginning assigned responsibilities. Maintain appropriate confidentiality regarding students, families, and ministry matters. Communicate concerns, incidents, or student needs promptly to Student Ministries for leadership. Exercise Biblically-sound judgment and responsibility during ministry events, transportation, and community activities. QUALIFICATIONS & REQUIREMENTS Faith & Ministry Commitment Profess a personal faith in Jesus Christ and demonstrate a commitment to ongoing spiritual growth and Christian community. Be actively involved in a church, campus ministry, or other Christian community. Demonstrate an understanding of foundational biblical principles and a willingness to share the Gospel. Have a genuine desire to invest in the spiritual growth and development of middle school and high school students. Support the mission, values, and ministry philosophy of Colonial Presbyterian Church. Skills & Abilities Strong interpersonal and communication skills, particularly when working with middle school and high school students. Demonstrated leadership potential, initiative, and a willingness to learn. Organizational skills and the ability to assist with planning and coordinating ministry activities. Ability to work collaboratively, receive feedback, and adapt to changing ministry needs. Dependability, maturity, and sound judgment when working with students. Additional Requirements College-aged student or young adult with an interest in Christian ministry. Availability to participate in the full nine-week summer program, including required training, events, and ministry activities. Willingness and ability to live in Colonial-provided community housing during the internship. Valid driver's license and reliable access to transportation. Successful completion of required background screening and child protection training. SCHEDULE & PROGRAM EXPECTATIONS The Summer Staff Internship is a nine-week program that includes scheduled ministry activities, leadership development, community living, and student engagement. Afternoons and Evenings: Student discipleship, relational ministry, small groups, events, and outreach activities. Sundays: Participation in assigned student ministry programming and church activities. Fridays and Saturdays: Generally designated as days off, subject to scheduled ministry activities and program requirements. The specific schedule will be established and communicated by Student Ministries leadership. COMPENSATION & PROGRAM BENEFITS Colonial's Summer Staff Internship provides an opportunity to gain practical ministry experience while participating in intentional leadership and spiritual development. Program offerings include: Competitive compensation for the nine-week internship. Church-provided community housing and meals. Gas reimbursement in accordance with Colonial's reimbursement guidelines. Two regularly scheduled days off each week, generally Friday and Saturday. Juneteenth and Independence Day holidays off, as scheduled by the ministry. Opportunity to participate in a summer camp alongside students and ministry staff. Leadership development seminars with experienced Kansas City leaders. CPR and First Aid training. End-of-summer team retreat at Lake of the Ozarks focused on rest, celebration, and reflection. PHYSICAL & WORK ENVIRONMENT This position involves indoor and outdoor ministry activities, group events, recreational activities, occasional travel, standing, walking, assisting with event setup, and supervising students. Interns must be able to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation. ADDITIONAL EXPECTATIONS As a ministry of Colonial Presbyterian Church, all Summer Staff Interns are expected to demonstrate Christ-centered character, maintain appropriate boundaries with students, and contribute positively to the mission and culture of the church. This position description outlines the general responsibilities and expectations of the internship and is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties. jobs.title: 2027 AKS Environmental Services Internship Program at AKS Engineering & Forestry LLC
jobs.description: Employer: AKS Engineering & Forestry LLC - AKS Expires: 12/10/2026 Go Beyond the Classroom Looking to build real-world experience this summer? The AKS Internship Program gives college students the chance to apply what they’re learning in the classroom, build practical skills, and contribute in a professional environment. Through meaningful project experience and a supportive team setting, interns gain confidence, broaden their understanding of the industry, and take important steps toward career readiness. How it WorksEach internship experience may look a little different depending on the role and team, but every internship is designed to help students learn by doing. Interns gain hands-on experience through real work, connect with professionals across AKS, and get a better understanding of how different disciplines contribute to project outcomes. For students who return, each summer can build on the last with new experiences, added responsibility, and a deeper understanding of areas that interest them. Participation is a one-summer commitment at a time. Students who are interested in returning are encouraged to express interest, and continued participation depends on performance, program fit, and available positions. Who You AreTo be considered for this internship program, students should: Be currently enrolled in an accredited 2- or 4-year program with a declared major in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Geology, or similar. Have completed at least one year of college before the internship start date Maintain a GPA of 3.0 or higher Be available to work full-time for 12 weeks during the summer Be able to work from the Las Vegas, NV office, where this program is offered Have a valid driver’s license What You’ll LearnEnvironmental Planning & Permitting: Gain an understanding of environmental requirements for energy and infrastructure projects, including NEPA, federal permitting, right-of-way authorizations, agency requirements, and permitting strategies. Environmental Surveys & Field Studies: Gain practical experience supporting environmental surveys, field studies, critical issue analyses, and environmental due diligence while learning how environmental conditions influence project planning and development. Environmental Compliance & Agency Coordination: Learn how environmental requirements are carried through project development and construction through monitoring, compliance activities, agency coordination, documentation, and communication with project stakeholders. Day in the Life (Examples)Work under the direction of a Project Manager and alongside the Environmental team to gain hands-on experience in a client-focused consulting environment. Interns can expect to work approximately 40-50 hours per week while contributing to project work and day-to-day team priorities. Responsibilities may include: Assisting with environmental research, desktop reviews, critical issues analyses, and due diligence activities to identify potential environmental constraints and project risks. Supporting the preparation and organization of environmental documentation, including NEPA materials, permit applications, agency correspondence, technical reports, maps, and other project deliverables. Participating in environmental surveys, field studies, monitoring, and site visits as appropriate, documenting field observations and assisting with data collection and organization. Supporting agency coordination, permitting, and environmental compliance activities by tracking requirements, maintaining project records, monitoring action items, and assisting project teams with regulatory deadlines and deliverables. We Have Your Back At AKS, interns are supported throughout the summer. Each intern is paired with a mentor and receives direction from a supervisor who guides assignments and project work. That supervisor may vary depending on the projects involved. Throughout the internship, interns receive regular feedback to support learning, growth, and professional development. At the end of the summer, each intern participates in a final evaluation to reflect on their experience, discuss future goals, and explore the possibility of returning for another internship, based on performance and available openings. Earn While You Learn This is a paid internship, and interns are compensated for their time and contributions. Pay is provided on an hourly basis, with overtime paid at one and a half times the regular rate for hours worked over 40 in a week. The typical pay range for this position is $19 to $25 per hour. Time off may be requested in advance, but it is unpaid.

jobs.title: Director of Landsports at Camp Pinecliffe
jobs.description: Employer: Camp Pinecliffe Expires: 12/12/2026 Position OverviewCamp Pinecliffe is seeking an energetic, highly organized, and passionate Director of Landsports for the upcoming summer season. This role is ideal for upperclassmen or graduating seniors majoring in Physical Education, Kinesiology, or Sports Management who want to gain invaluable, hands-on athletic leadership experience while earning internship credit.Our program serves approximately 200 female campers ages 7–15. As Director, you will put your PE coursework into real-world practice by managing all land athletic facilities, leading and mentoring a dedicated team of student coaches, designing age-appropriate skill progressions, organizing large-group recreational PE games, coordinating signature camp athletic events, and maintaining top safety standards across all disciplines.Key ResponsibilitiesProgram Leadership & Athletic InstructionMulti-Sport Curriculum: Oversee the design and implement structured, high-energy daily instruction across soccer, basketball, softball, volleyball, archery, gymnastics, lacrosse, and field hockey. Making sure each individual sport coach is prepared for their daily lessons.Differentiated Coaching: Adapt athletic instruction to developmental age groups.Character Development & Sportsmanship: Emphasize personal growth, athletic integrity, resilience, fair play, and positive encouragement across all skill levels.Staff Supervision & Team LeadershipStaff Mentorship & Management: Direct, evaluate, and mentor 6-10 landsports counselors and activity instructors. Assign court/field leads, provide ongoing coaching feedback, and ensure energetic camper engagement.Scheduling & Rotations: Work with the Program Office to establish daily staff duty rotations, field assignments, supervisory coverage, and off-period management.Safety & Conduct: Enforce strict safety protocols across all fields and courts (including equipment checks, spectator boundaries, hydration/heat protocols, and sunscreen enforcement).Camp Traditions & Special Events100-Mile Club & Track Events: Oversee the tracking and recording of camper miles for the annual 100-Mile Club and organize Track & Field day activities.Inter-Camp & Intra-Camp Competition: Roster, prepare, and coach Pinecliffe teams for inter-camp athletic matches with neighboring camps, as well as internal Color War competitions.Inclement Weather Programming: Implement energetic rainy day/indoor alternative plans (gym games, indoor team building, or waterfront adaptations) when fields are unusable.Field Maintenance & Equipment CareFacility Preparation: Oversee daily setup and field checks for soccer, softball, lacrosse, field hockey, basketball, volleyball, and archery zones prior to morning sessions.Inventory & Gear Care: Manage sports equipment inventory, organize storage sheds, maintain sign-out logs, inspect gear for safety hazards, and report facility repair needs. Ensure all equipment is properly put away at the end of the day.Department AdministrationPre-Camp Staff Training: Participate in leadership orientation and lead the Landsports staff in setting up fields, equipment, lesson planning, and practical instructional strategies ahead of camper arrival.End-of-Season Report: Prepare a thorough end-of-summer department report summarizing camper achievements, staff evaluations, equipment counts, field maintenance needs, and recommendations for future seasons.Qualifications & RequirementsEducation & Experience: Currently enrolled upperclassman (junior/senior) or recent graduate in Physical Education, Kinesiology, Sports Leadership, or related field. Prior experience coaching youth sports or leading recreational programs is preferred.Broad Sport Knowledge: Multi-sport competency across major team sports (soccer, basketball, softball, lacrosse, field hockey, volleyball) and individual activities (archery, gymnastics) is a plus, but not necessary.Leadership & Team Management: Demonstrated ability to manage, inspire, and evaluate a young adult coaching staff.Communication & Leadership: Strong motivation to lead peers, exceptional communication skills, highly energetic approach, and a passion for empowering young female athletes.Physical Stamina: Ability to coach outdoors on fields and courts in summer weather conditions for full camp operating hours.Compensation & BenefitsSalary: Competitive seasonal salary commensurate with leadership experience.Room & Board: Full housing and all daily meals provided on-site for the duration of the contract.Travel Allowance: Travel stipend or travel reimbursement provided.Professional Growth: Hands-on executive management experience directing a major athletic department within a prestigious residential camp.Internship Credit & Practical Hours: Fulfills field experience/practicum hours or senior internship course requirements for Physical Education and Sports Management majors, with official performance evaluations provided.About Camp PinecliffeFounded in 1917, Camp Pinecliffe is a traditional, four-generation, family-owned, all-girls residential camp located on Crystal Lake in Harrison, Maine. Pinecliffe provides a warm, supportive community for girls ages 7–15, focusing on developing confidence, independence, character, and lifelong friendships through diverse athletic, waterfront, outdoor adventure, and creative arts programs.

jobs.title: Museum Education Intern at The Bakken Museum
jobs.description: Employer: The Bakken Museum Expires: 12/12/2026 Museum Education InternHOW TO APPLY:Please email Anika Taylor taylor@thebakken.org with the following information.1. Two to three paragraphs in the body of the email detailing why you are interested in this position and how you meet the requirements described in this job description. Each paragraph should be between 3-7 sentences, for a total length of no more than 21 sentences. Do not attach a cover letter. 2. Your resume or work/skills/training history as an attachment or a link to your LinkedIn profile in your email response. We do not have a preference. Our aim is to understand where you have worked and the types of roles you have had. 3. OPTIONAL – Please consider filling out an optional, anonymous demographics survey, found here (https://thebakkenmuseum.formstack.com/forms/igm_applicant_demographic_survey). This survey will remain unattached to any application materials and is used only to determine patterns and opportunities for improvement. The hiring manager will not have access to the individual responses collected.Complete applications will receive confirmation of submission within 72 hours. Application deadline is December 7th. Please contact Anika Taylor if you have questions about this process.JOB DESCRIPTION: Department: Education Reports to: Field Trip Programs Coordinator Compensation: $500 Stipend Grade: N/A Educational/Degree Requirement: None Exempt or Nonexempt: Nonexempt Hourly or Salaried: N/A Hours Per Week: 5-10 (flexible) Hybrid or On Site: On Site Language proficiency: English. Proficiency/familiarity with another language is a plus but not required. Schedule: VariesWHO WE ARE AND WHAT WE DO: The Bakken Museum is a one-of-a-kind museum with a focus on innovation and the intersection of STEM and the humanities. The museum encourages curiosity through our exhibitions, events, and on and off-site education programs. Our purpose is to awaken the innovator inside each of us.OUR VALUES: Curiosity: Wonder by asking bold questions, challenging assumptions, and seeking new perspectives. Center diverse voices to ensure exploration is equitable and relevant. Creativity: Try and discover by generating, testing, and refining ideas. Take risks, learn from failure, and think outside of the box to create solutions that reveal unique possibilities. Collaboration: Share by combining strengths, engaging partners, and building toward shared outcomes. Work across teams, communities, and volunteers to co-create adaptable solutions that are stronger, more inclusive, and more impactful together.EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER: The Bakken provides equal employment opportunities for all persons regardless of age, race, color, religion, creed, national origin, marital status, familial status, sex, gender identity and/or expression, pregnancy, sexual orientation, disability, veteran status, genetic information, status with regard to public assistance, or any other characteristic protected under federal, state, or local law. Equal employment opportunity applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leave of absence, compensation, and training.POSITION OVERVIEW: The Education Intern helps with museum education programs, including giving tours, supporting classroom programs, completing clerical tasks, and collecting audience and program data. This role will be split between direct contact time with students, teachers, and other museum audience as well as behind the scenes program support.ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES PERCENT OF ROLE Museum Education Programs • Supports during education classroom programs • Delivers tours to field trips groups • Collects surveys and observational data from various museum audiences 70% Museum Support Tasks • Supports daily museum tasks ie clerical work or floor facilitation 30% Other duties as needed or required: Perform other duties as needed or required which are within the position's scope. Diversity, equity, accessibility, and inclusion Diversity, equity, accessibility, and inclusion (DEAI) are core functions of all positions at the Bakken Museum. While some roles may have more specific responsibilities, the items below are a part of everyone's role at the museum: • Demonstrate a commitment to DEAI through continuous personal development, modeling inclusive behaviors, and proactively managing bias to help cultivate and promote a culture of inclusivity and belonging for all staff.• Proactively work on your own and collaboratively with other museum staff to ensure equitable and representative experiences for all museum visitors and program participants.POSITION REQUIREMENTS: • Comfort interacting with a large variety of people in a potentially busy or noisy space. • Comfort in delivering material to an elementary-aged audience in a clear and engaging way. • Ability to travel to the museum in a timely manner. • Strong listener, giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand, and asking questions as appropriate. Ability to work independently and as part of a team. • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.PHYSICAL DEMANDS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions. • Ability to sit and/or stand for up to 8 hours per shift. • Ability to move through and access all areas of the buildings and grounds including stairs, indoor and outdoor areas, and small spaces. • Ability to manipulate computers, office equipment, folding chairs and tables, and similar items related to an office environment.TRAVEL: None.The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by the staff member assigned to this position. This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.
